key_insight: A hybrid β-VAE-GAN plus sensor-conditioned Transformer can compress and forecast intermittent near-wall turbulence in the Minimal Flow Unit from sparse measurements with physically meaningful latent variables.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reduced-order surrogate that could enable long-horizon prediction and control of wall-bounded turbulent flows at far lower computational cost than full CFD.
method: β-VAE-GAN compresses high-dimensional flow fields into a 4D latent space.
Easy Attention Transformer predicts latent evolution from sparse sensor inputs.
AdaLN-Zero modulates the temporal model using sensor conditioning.
evidence_signal: On the Minimal Flow Unit at Reτ=200 and y+=14, the model recovers 87% of turbulent kinetic energy in the compressed representation and achieves 82% TKE reconstruction over 17,288 t+ from a 128 t+ initialization window.
watch_item: Rare high-amplitude events are attenuated, so extreme intermittent bursts may be underpredicted in low-dimensional latent bottlenecks.
paper_title: A Hybrid Generative Reduced-Order Model for the Minimal Flow Unit
